provenance.paper_title: MovieChat: From Dense Token to Sparse Memory for Long Video Understanding

latest_version.version_label: arXiv current version served on review date

evidence.section: Full paper: 2.3. Memory Models in Vision Tasks
evidence.paraphrase: A bounded short-term buffer stores frame-level visual feature tokens and periodically transfers them for consolidation.
Adjacent visual tokens are iteratively merged by similarity and the sparse result is appended to long-term memory.

evidence.section: Full-paper method / memory representation and retrieval
evidence.paraphrase: Global and breakpoint modes activate the stored visual representation through projection into the language model; no source-frame lookup is defined.

A fixed, parameter-free consolidation rule repeatedly merges the most similar adjacent frame tokens. For MovieChat, this specifically supports merging or deduplication of overlapping entries of short-term and long-term memory.

evidence.section: Full paper: 2.3. Memory Models in Vision Tasks
evidence.paraphrase: Compressed short-term tokens are appended to long-term memory and initialize the next short-term segment, explicitly migrating state between tiers. For MovieChat, this specifically supports migration between memory tiers of short-term and long-term memory.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 4): During inference, the operative memory component (short-term and long-term memory) changes through merging or deduplication of overlapping entries, migration between memory tiers; the governing policy remains fixed, and any learning reported by the paper occurs before deployment. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
